body: We are about to request renewal of our DigitalOcean sponsorship, and they have previously asked if we could mention them in the project's README, so let's do that. The assets are taken from [DigitalOcean Open Source Sponsorship Attribution Guide](https://opensource.nyc3.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com/attribution/index.html). I wanted to make the image to better align with the text within the sponsors list, but GitHub removes any html `style=` formatting, so I had to make the image a bit smaller than suggested in the DO's attribution guide, 201px -> 151px, to make the misalignment less horrible to look at while not making the image way too small. Although the README hotlinks the svg off DigitalOcean, GitHub proxies images for privacy's sake, so the hotlinking shouldn't be an issue. Somewhat inspired by how [AFLplusplus](https://aflplus.plus) mentions their sponsors at the end of the homepage, though I have put the sponsor's image at the front. I have used this opportunity to also mention other tools and services we use by making an Acknowledgments list. Say if I have missed anything on it. iphy and I have discussed making this PR about a year ago, right after we have renewed the DO sponsorship the last time, so better late than never. Q: Should we keep the "SAST Tools" section which is above, or is it now redundant due to the Acknowledgments section also listing the static analyzers? Note that I have omitted listing TokTok's own tools under Acknowledgments (which the SAST Tools section does list), since it's kind of weird to be thanking ourselves, but I can see an argument for adding them to the list for sake of visibility. Would be nice if we could get this merged before April. Technically our DigitalOcean credits already expired on March 27th, so I have to re-apply for the sponsorship very soon and want to be able to link them the README with DO being credited as the sponsor on it when re-applying. - - - This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/TokTok/c-toxcore/3031)

comment_regular_data.body:
> a number of excellent tools and services

Putting our own tools under here feels kinda odd.

Hah, that's funny.

The 32-bit iOS CI was failing to build libsodium, so I have sent a fix to TokTok/dockerfiles. I decided to test it in here via https://github.com/TokTok/c-toxcore/commit/d18ee91fe73b93c993842763d67886c57760a334, as it would be annoying if that doesn't actually fix it or if there is more stuff to fix. By me testing the fix in here, libsodium got built successfully and got cached. So now that I have removed the test CI fix commit, the CI no longer fails because libsodium got cached in this PR's GitHub Actions cache from when the fix commit was still in.

Basically, CI side-effects via force-push commits and CI caching.

(Well, maybe it's not funny to you, but it was funny to me, because after I have removed the test fix commit, I was extremely confused, like "Huh? Why is the CI no longer failing? It should be failing, I removed the commit fixing the failure. Huh?" and then it hit me as to what might be going on, and I had to verify that the CI does indeed skip the dep building now that the iOS build got its deps cached.)

Anyone knows why is bazel not happy and how to fix it? I don't use bazel so it's not very obvious to me.

>FATAL: corrupt installation: file '/home/builder/.cache/bazel/_bazel_builder/install/e34c151ba748177908efa53a79278e09/A-server.jar' is missing or modified.  Please remove '/home/builder/.cache/bazel/_bazel_builder/install/e34c151ba748177908efa53a79278e09' and try again.

Does that cache come from the script downloading https://github.com/TokTok/toktok-stack/releases/download/nightly/asan.tar?
I need to fix bazel. Until then, let's make it non blocking.

>let's make it non blocking.

Sounds good. I think only you have the ability to make the CI checks non-required though.

Unless I'm missing something, it doesn't look like hs-github-tools's CI is setup to automatically apply the repo settings, so I assume you (@iphydf) run the script setting those settings up yourself, locally, using your GitHub token. Also, how come the repo settings as described in hs-github-tools don't seem to be the actual settings currently in use? It lists "ci / analysis (tokstyle)" as a required check for c-toxcore, yet I can see that it is no required in this PR. Did someone manually edit c-toxcore's branch protection or forgot to push the modified repos file?

hs-github-tools aside, I also can't do it manually as I don't have access to the "Branch protection rules" section of the Settings of the c-toxcore repository.
